thread:
Maya: quick callout — we need to pick sequencing for rollout/canary controls: implement a minimal API-first surface (programmatic canaries + flags) vs shipping a console-first experience (visual canary config, history, diff). Acme asked for console UI but legal wants programmatic hooks. what do we prioritize?
Devon: API-first leans into dev friction == lower. We can ship hooks + stable schema faster. Console can follow as an ops/PM feature.
Samir: engineering reality — API-only still needs: rollout engine work, audit logs, backing storage, and trace integration. effort ~= 6 sprint-weeks across runtime + infra. Console UI itself is ~3-4 sprints but many infra pieces overlap.
li-wei: from design — console reduces support calls and makes advanced configs discoverable. customers who are non-devs will struggle w/ API-only.
olivia: commercial note: Acme will expand contract if console is available. They asked directly. However several smaller customers just want API hooks. Tradeoff: >$500k ARR opportunity vs many quick wins.
nash (prod-bot): created checklist: security review, audit log schema, canary metrics, rollback policy.
nash (prod-bot): reminder: SLA addendum required for console-based rollouts.
nash (prod-bot): added integrations: prometheus, datadog, trace export.
Ashish: threw together a quick RICE sketch to make this concrete:
```
Option                      Reach   Impact   Confidence   Effort   RICE
API-minimal                 8      6        0.8          3        128
Console-full                4      8        0.6          8         24
API+lite-console (phased)   7      7        0.7          5         69
```
Ashish: notes: reach = number of customer segments, impact = internal score, effort in sprint-weeks, confidence rough. numbers are intentionally coarse to prompt discussion.
Devon: I trust this. API-minimal gives fastest unblock for feature teams building canaries in their apps. Also easier to A/B rollout.
Samir: caution — API-minimal creates surface area we must support forever. Without console, we'll get lots of bespoke scripts supported by SRE. Long term ops cost > dev cost.
li-wei: compromise: ship API-minimal + an opinionated "Canary overview" micro-console (single-page, read+history, basic controls) — gives discoverability but keeps scope small.
olivia: that feels like it preserves Acme upside (we can sell roadmap + console later) and delivers something visible now.
Maya: proposed launch criteria:
- API spec stable and documented (openapi)
- Audit logs + trace export enabled
- Canary metrics surfaced in Console micro-view
- Beta customers (2) onboarded
If we hit these, we GA minimal API + micro-console.
Devon: rough schedule: API-minimal + infra (3 sprints), micro-console (2 sprints) after. can parallelize docs + SDKs.
Samir: ok but need canary rollout sim tests + perf guardrails before GA. add to criteria.
li-wei: will draft micro-console wireframes by EOW.
olivia: i'll confirm Acme beta + put note in contract about console roadmap.
Ashish: action items captured: scope API schema, infra tickets for audit/log, micro-console MVP wireframes, sales commit. I'll update roadmap entry and RICE score after dev estimates.
Maya: consensus seems to lean phased approach (API-first + lightweight console). thumbs? :thumbsup: for phased, :thumbsdown: for console-first, :hand: for API-only
Devon: :thumbsup:
Samir: :thumbsup:
li-wei: :thumbsup:
olivia: :thumbsup:
Ashish: :thumbsup:
Maya: cool — moving to phased plan. I'll schedule a quick sync with eng leads and PMs tomorrow 10am to finalize estimates. Thanks everyone!
